name: Real-time clock DS3231 mini module (14 x 14 mm, no LED)
description: The small DS3231 board sold for the Raspberry Pi: the same accurate clock chip as the ZS-042 (I2C 0x68, RTClib RTC_DS3231) on a 14 x 14 mm board with its coin cell on top, no power LED and no charging circuit, so it draws only the chip's 0.11 mA. Wire + → 3V3, D → SDA, C → SCL, − → GND (NC stays free). For a thin case cut the 5-pin socket off and solder wires (it then stands about 6 mm).

pins.description: Supply, 2.3 to 5.5 V (Pi header pin 1, 3.3 V).

pins.label: D
pins.description: I2C data (Pi pin 3). Pi modules often have no pull-up resistors (the Pi has its own): check yours, and add 4.7 kOhm from SDA and SCL to 3V3 if it has none.

pins.label: NC
pins.description: Not connected on the module (Pi pin 7).

props.label: Time at t = 0
props.description: Clock time when the simulation starts. A scenario's clock and set_clock set it too; the sketch can call rtc.adjust().

props.label: Temperature
props.description: Die temperature the RTC reports (registers 0x11/0x12, 0.25 °C steps).

props.label: Lost power
props.description: Start with the oscillator-stop flag set, as after the coin cell ran out (RTClib rtc.lostPower() returns true).

footprint: 14 x 14 mm module, 5-pin 0.1 in female socket for Pi header pins 1-9, coin-cell holder on top

bindings.description: HH:MM:SS shown on the module drawing.
Powered (it keeps time on its coin cell, but answers I2C only when powered).

mechanical.source: seller listings (pishop.co.za, hotmcu.com): 14 x 14 x 12 mm with the 5-pin socket; measure yours, the coin cell sits on top

sourcing.generic: DS3231 mini RTC module for Raspberry Pi (DS3231SN, coin cell on top, no LED), 14 x 14 mm
